records.title: Empowered Women Empower Communities

_annotations.body:
Empowered Women Empower Communities
Women are the backbone of agriculture in India, and that is no exaggeration. They play a pivotal role in agriculture: 85% of rural women in our country are engaged in agricultural activities, and 75% of the farmers in the agriculture field are women. In addition, women are also responsible for the majority of household chores, such as cooking and taking care of children. Despite their efforts, they are hardly recognised as farmers and in most the communities, d power largely lies with the men of the household. Women have restricted mobility, and require permission from their elders and husband. Their stake in intra-household decision making still remains a grey area and is a deep-rooted issue that needs to be worked upon.

Innovation: Digital Green's Video-Based Agricultural Extension

Description: Digital Green pioneered a video-enabled approach to agricultural extension where local community members create and share educational videos featuring fellow farmers demonstrating improved agricultural practices. The videos are shown in small community groups using battery-operated projectors, followed by discussions facilitated by local resource persons.

This qualifies as an innovation because:

1. It meets several of the listed criteria:
- Creates more equitable business models by empowering local communities to create and share knowledge
- Accelerates participatory approaches through community-led content creation
- Enhances inclusion and equity by making agricultural knowledge accessible to illiterate farmers
- Focuses on socio-cultural aspects by featuring local farmers in locally relevant contexts
- Supports behavioral change through peer-to-peer learning
- Has strong grassroots participation in content creation and dissemination

2. It represents a novel application of technology (video) to transform traditional agricultural extension services by:
- Making knowledge transfer more engaging and effective
- Enabling scale through digital replication
- Leveraging social learning through peer demonstration
- Preserving local knowledge while introducing improved practices
- Reducing costs compared to traditional extension methods

The approach has been recognized as innovative by multiple organizations including the World Bank and FAO, and has demonstrated significant impact in improving agricultural practices and productivity across multiple countries.

The concept of user-generated content has seeped into and transformed traditional information dissemination channels for the rural population. Stepping out of the passive consumption mode, rural community members are now playing an active role in developing and sharing content on improved practices and behaviors within their immediate network. Much like urban folks who are influenced by peers on social networks and add their own 'Like' or RT to help a meme or video go viral, farmers tend to be convinced of the benefits of a practice when a fellow farmer promotes it - convinced enough to adopt the practice and help spread the word within their own groups.Â
